column2: Then he should perform the six-limb rite: Surya, Soma, Niranjana, Nirabhasa, Dharma and Jnana, in turn, as well as the others.
In order, with "Hamsa" at the start and the middle-voice words at the end, joined with the class-terms, the best of practitioners should apply these to the six limbs.
The syllable "ha", with splendour like the sun, goes out; "sa" likewise; meditation on entry is declared.
Having so meditated, the wise one should offer in parts to the fires and suns: in the muladhara, with the four-petalled seed beginning "va" and ending "sa",
bandhuka-red, together with his power, to him who rides on the water, whose hand holds noose, goad, nectar-vessel and sweets,
he should offer six hundred to Ganesha and the lord of speech. In the svadhishthana, coral-coloured, with the syllables "va" to "la",
to the lord of learning with his power on his left, to the lotus-born with ladle and rosary in shining hands,
to Brahma riding the swan, he should offer six thousand. In the manipura, with lightning-bright cloud colour, with petals "da" to "pha",
to Vishnu bearing conch, discus, mace and lotus, with Shri, he should offer six thousand.
In the anahata, twelve-petalled, with syllables "ka" to "tha", white, to the one holding trident, boon, protection and nectar-pot,
with his power on his left, the lord of learning, the wise one should offer to Rudra riding the bull six thousand.
In the vishuddha, sixteen-petalled, rich in vowels, white, to the great-luminous lord of the senses,
joined with prana-shakti, he should offer a thousand. In the ajna wheel, with "ha" and "ksha", the two-petalled lotus, a thousand,
to Sadashiva, the teacher, with Para-shakti. In the thousand-petalled great lotus with nada and bindu,
shining with the letters of the alphabet, to the one whose hands give boons, to the primal teacher, he should offer a thousand.
Taking water in the palm again, spontaneously the accomplished; of the twenty-one thousand six hundred repetitions...
of this Ajapa, in divisions, by resolve: "May Vishnu, giver of liberation, be pleased with me."
By the mere resolve of it one is freed from great sins: "I am Brahman, not a transmigrator, eternally free, not subject to grief,
I am of the nature of being-consciousness-bliss" — so he should meditate on the Self. Then he should perform bodily duties and worship of the gods.
I shall tell its procedure and the marks of good conduct.
The eight Mothers beginning with Brahmi, as powers, stand at the doors themselves; with the Moon, their own names beginning "gharna", ending in "namah" are held.
Then, seated on a seat, the wise one, having sipped water, pure, having driven away with effort obstacles divine, atmospheric and earthly,
the best Vaishnava should place the Keshava-matrika (the alphabet-deities): Keshava with Kirti, Narayana with Kanti,
Madhava with Tushti, Govinda with Pushti, Vishnu with Dhriti, Madhusudana with Shanti,
Trivikrama with Kriya, Vamana with Dayita, Shridhara with Medha, Hrishikesha with Harsha,
Padmanabha with Shraddha, Damodara with Lajja, Vasudeva with Lakshmi, Sankarshana with Sarasvati,
Pradyumna with Priti, Aniruddha with Rati, the Discus-bearer with Jaya, then Mace-bearer with Durga,
the Bow-bearer with Prabha, Sword-bearer with Satya, Conch-bearer with Chanda, Plough-bearer with Vani,
Pestle-bearer with Vilasini, Trident-bearer with Vijaya, Noose-bearer with Viraja, Goad-bearer with Vishvasa,
Mukunda with Vinata, Nandaja with Sunanda, Nandin with Smriti, Nara with Vriddhi,
Hari with Samriddhi, Narakajit with Shuddhi; Krishna with Buddhi, Satya with Bhukti, Sattvata with Mukti,
Shauri with ... Janardana with Uma; Bhudhara with Kledini; Vishvamurti with Klinna,
Vaikuntha with Vasudha; Purushottama with Vasuda; Bali with Para; (Balanuja with ...),
... Vrishaghna with Sandhya; Vrisha with Prajna; Hamsa with Prabha; Varaha with Nisha;
Vimala with Dhara; Nrisimha with Vidyut. The sage of the Keshava-matrika is held to be Narayana.
The metre is Amritadya Gayatri, the deity Vishnu. One should worship Hari endowed with discus and other weapons, holding a pot and mirror,
with Lakshmi, bright as lightning, with many ornaments. Having thus meditated, he should place the power, the syllable enclosed by "shri" and "kama".
With Vishnu and Shakti he should say "heart" with Om at the start. He should assign skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and semen to the life-breaths.
Prana and anger, and in the ten beginning with "ma", "bhya": one on the head, one on the face, two on the eyes, two on the ears,
two on the nostrils, two on the cheeks, two on the lips, one at the root of the tongue and one on the neck.
He should place the "ka" series on the right arm, the "cha" series on the left arm, the "ta" and "ta" series on the feet, and "pa" and "pha" on the two sides.
On the spine "va"; on the navel "bha"; on the heart "ma"; the seven beginning with "ya" in the constituents; "ha" in the breath, "la" in the self,
ksha in anger: placing them in order, one becomes able to worship Vishnu. With Purnodari, Shrikantha; Ananta with Vija...
Sukshmesha with Shalmali; Trimata with Lolakshi; Maheshvara with Vartulakshi; the lord ... with Dirghaghona;
Bharabhuti with Dirghamukhi; Tithisha with Gomukhi; Sthaveresha with Dirghajihva; Dhara with Kudodari;
Jhintisha with Urdhvakeshi; Bhautika with Vikritasya; Sadya with Jvalamukhi; Anugraha with Ulkamukhi;
Akrura with Asya; Mahasena with Vidya; Krodhisha with Mahakali; Sarasvati with Chandesha;
Panchantaka with Siddhagauri; then Shirottama; Trailokyavidya; Ekarudra with Mantrashakti;
Kurmesha with Kamathi; Ekanetra with Bhutamatra; Chaturvaktra with Lambodari; Ajesha with Dravini;
Sarvesha with Nagari; Somesha with Khecari; Langalisha with Maryada; Rupini with Darukesha;
Ardhanarisha with Varuni; Umakanta with Gunishvara; Kakodari; Ashadhi; with Putana;
Dandisha with Bhadrakali; ... with Yogini; Minesha with Shankhini; Meshesha with Tarjani;
Lohita with Kalaratri; Shikhisha with Kujani; Chhalaganda with Kapardini; Dviranda with Vajra;
Mahabala with Jaya; Balisha with Sumukheshvari; Bhujanga with Revati; Pinaki with Madhavi;
Khadgisha with Varuni; Bakesha with Vayavi; Shvetoraska with Vidarini; Bhrigu with Sahaja;
Lakulisha with Lakshmi; Shivesha with Vyapini; in Samvartaka, Mahamaya. Thus is declared the Shrikantha-matrika.
Where the word "svisha" (own lord) is not said, one should supply it everywhere. The sage is Dakshinamurti; the metre is said to be Gayatri;
the deity is Ardhanarishvara; the application is for obtaining all. The consonants are the seeds; the vowels are the powers.
He should make the limbs with the "bhrigu" syllable joined with space and enriched with six long vowels; body bandhuka-gold in colour, with boon, rosary, goad and noose,
crowned with a half-moon, three-eyed, worshipped by gods: he should contemplate. Having meditated thus, Shiva and Shakti and the fourth case, ending in "heart".
He should place, in the place of the alphabet, with the sau seed before the alphabet. Vighnesha with Hri; Vighnaraja with Shri;
Vinayaka with Pushti; Shivottama with Shanti; Vighnakrit with Svasti; Vighnahartri with Sarasvati;
Ganapati with Svaha; Ekadanta with Sumedha; Dvidanta with Kanti; Gajavakra with Kamini;
Niranjana with Mohini; Kapardin with Nati; Dirghajihva with Parvati; Shankukarna with Jvalini;
Vrishadhvaja with Nanda; Ganayaka with Sureshi; Gajendra with Kamarupini; Shurpakarna with Uma;
Virochana with Tejovati; Lambodara with Satya; Mahananda with Vighneshi; Chaturmurti with Svarupini;
Sadashiva with Kamada; Amoda with Madajihva; Dumukha with Bhuti; Sumukha with Bhautiki;
Pramodadha with Sita; Ekapada with Rama; Dvijihva with Mahishi; Shura with Jabhini;
Vira with Vikarna; Shanmukha with Bhrikuti; Varada with Lajja; Vamadeva with Dirghaghona;
Vakratunda with Dhanurdhari; Dviranda with Yamini; Senani with Ratri; Kamandha with Gramani;
Matta with Shashiprabha; Vimatta with Lolanetra; Mattavahana with Chanchala; Jati with Dipti;
Mundi with Subhaga; Khadgi with Durbhaga; Vareṇya with Shiva; Vrishaketana with Bhaga;
Bhakshyapriya with Bhagini; Ganesha with Bhagini; Meghanada with Subhaga; Vyapin with Kalaratri;
Ganeshvara with Kalinka — thus the Mothers of Vighnesha are declared. The group of the Ganesha-matrika is told by the sages.
The metre is Trivrit Gayatri; the deity is Shakti-Ganeshvara. Having made the limbs with the seed rich in six long vowels, he should then remember:
bearing noose, goad, protection and boon, with a lotus in the hand of his wife, embraced by his wife, red-bodied, three-eyed — thus Ganapati should be.
Having meditated thus, he should place it with his own seed's first letter. Nivritti, Pratishtha, Vidya, Shanti and others:
Dipika, Rechika, Mochika, Para; Sukshma, Asukshma, Amrita, Jnanamrita, Apyayini;
Vyapini, Vyomarupa, Ananta, Srishti, Samriddhika; Smriti, Medha, Kanti, Lakshmi, Dhriti, Sthira, Sthiti;
Siddhi, Jara, Palini, Kshanti, Ishvarika, Rati; Kamika, Varada, Hladini, Priti;
Dirgha, Tikshna, Raudra, Nidra, Tandrika; Kshudha, Krodhini, Kriyakari, Mrityuka;
Pita, Sveta, Aruna, then Asita, with Ananta: thus the Kala-matrika is declared; each devotee should practise it accordingly.
The sage of the Kala-matrika is said to be Prajapati; the metre is Gayatri, and the deity is named Sharada.
With Om-seeds in the short and long intervals he should perform the six limbs. Holding a lotus, wheel, rosary and deer-mark, three-eyed,
five-faced Bharati adorned with pearls — the wise man should worship her. Having thus meditated, he should place her preceded by Om with the Kalas.
Then he should perform the six limbs of the root mantra. At the end of the heart and the rest, in the fourth case, joining the class-terms, he should place:
namah, svaha, vashat, hum, vaushat, phat are called the class-terms. Then, having meditated on the chosen deity adorned and armed,
having placed the six limbs in his form, he should begin worship.
Women, the old, the young and fools, in order, as in the knowledge they act; that is called "hard to understand".
Thus, however he can, the practitioner should perform worship; he who lacks worship of the gods surely goes to hell.
Having done the Vaishvadeva and the rest, he should feed the best Brahmins; after offering to the god, he should himself eat with his own people.
Having sipped water and purified his mouth, he should rest a while, and hear the Purana and the epics with his kin.
One who is able in all main rites and performs a substitute — the fruit does not occur for that ill-minded one, with full completion.
Thus pairs arise in twenty-six ways; he should satisfy them in order with seed-syllables beginning with their own names.
Together they are four hundred and forty-four. Having thus satisfied them, he then does it as before with the services,
prays for all desires, bows, and dismisses them. Each month from the fourth of the dark half of Bhadrapada, unwearied,
the mantra-knower, from sunrise until moonrise, should not sit on the ground, controlling his speech, acts and mind.
Then at moonrise the mantra-knower should worship the leader of the hosts by the rule stated before, with various flowers and offerings.
He should offer twenty-one sweets; before him he should chant the mantra a thousand and eight times.
Then with camphor, saffron, red flowers and sandal he should give the offering of arghya, to the root mantra ending in "ye" (dative): to Ganapati.
I prepare this arghya — ending with the heart, the arghya is approved. Having praised, bowed and dismissed, he should again worship the Moon.
Having given arghya four times and worshipped the teacher, from the offered sweets he should give half to a Brahmin.
The celibate, master of senses, should himself eat the half. The man who observes this vow properly for a year
gains sons, grandsons, happiness, wealth and health. If unable from sunrise, the mantra-knower should keep the vow from sunset
until moonrise by the rule given before; doing so he certainly gains the fruit stated.
Having made an image of Ganesha from elephant tusk, or monkey (wood), elephant-tusk, neem or white arka,
and having invoked him in it with the infusing of life, he worships it by rule when the Moon is seized by Rahu (eclipse),
and touches it fasting, holding it by the top-knot: he gains victory in gambling, dispute, battle and lawsuit.
The seed "Varaha" with bindu, then ... "Smriti", "mamsa", "indu", ... one should say in the group of ear-leavings (Ganesha).
Baka with long "va", for the great Yaksha, "yam" — the offering. This is called the offering-mantra; otherwise a syllable does not grant all desires.
Om, the seed of Bhuvaneshani, ending in his own seed: nine syllables. "Hasti", "Pishachi" he should write, and "Agni-sundari".
This nine-syllable mantra is declared giving all success to worshippers. With the words and the whole mantra, he should make the five limbs.
Everything else is the same as with the previous mantra, O Narada. Now I shall tell by rule the unsurpassed Vakratunda.
(Vakratunda mantra in coded seed-syllables: "toya", "vahni", "karna", "indu", "Hari", "dirgha", "darika", "vayu", "varma".)
Its sage is Bhargava, metre Anushtubh, deity Ganadhipa called Vakratunda; the seed "vam" is the power, and the armour again.
With the mantra-syllables with Om in the middle and adorned with the moon, having made the six limbs, on the brow, throat and heart,
he should place the mantra-letters at name, sign and place, and spread them throughout. He should worship the elephant-faced one, bright as the rising sun,
holding noose, goad, boon and protection, in red ornaments and clothes. Having so meditated, he should chant a hundred thousand and tenth part offerings of substances;
he should offer eight on the seat, worship with Tivra and the others. Imagining the form in his own form, he should invoke and worship there:
in the six corners, the six limbs; on the petals, the eight powers. He should worship Vidya, Vidhatri, Bhogada, Vipraghatini,
Nidhipradipa, Papaghni, Punya, then Shashiprabha. On the petal-tips: Vakratunda, Ekadamshtra, Mahodara,
Gajasya, Lambodara, Vikata, Vighnaraja, Dhumravarna; and outside, the guardians of the quarters with their weapons.
Having thus worshipped the leader of the hosts with five enclosures, the practitioner accomplishes all desires by Vakratunda's grace.
Having received the mantra from the teacher's mouth with the rite of initiation, as a celibate, eating havishya, truthful and master of senses,
he should chant a thousand (times) for six months, joined with fire-offerings; overcoming poverty he becomes like Kubera.
From the fourth to the next fourth, he should respectfully chant ten thousand; offering a hundred and eight daily he gets the fruit as before.
In both fortnights the mantra-knower should offer a hundred on the fourth with cakes; in a year he attains the supreme place of prosperity.
On a Tuesday fourth, having worshipped the god by rule, he should prepare an offering of havis and milk-rice.
Then, having honoured the teacher, the wise man should feed him by rule and offer a thousand oblations of the offered food into the fire by rule.
Having done so for a year, he attains great prosperity. Now I shall tell another practice, out of desire for the good of the world.
Having worshipped Ganesha with flattened rice, milk-rice, cakes and sweets, and various fruits, the practitioner
should chant the mantra over turmeric, rock salt, and a half-nishka of vacha, or half of that. Having purified the powder, he should put a handful in cow's urine,
and, having carefully recited the mantra over it a thousand times, on the day of her bath after menses, a pure woman in white clothes,
placed before the god, the wise man should give her the medicine to drink; even a barren woman obtains a son with all marks.
Now I shall tell another secret, supremely wonderful. Having carefully plastered a space of a cow-hide with cow-dung,
and strewn it with heaps of grain, he should place a pot there. Filling it with pure water, he should set it on top,
and on it a new auspicious dish full of ghee of a tawny cow. With the six- and eight-syllable mantras he should light an auspicious lamp.
Invoking the god in the lamp, he should worship with perfume, flowers and so on. The wise man should worship a bathed virgin or a boy.
Placing (the child) before the lamp and meditating on the god, he should chant the mantra. When the lamp is set, one sees Ganesha in the form of a Brahmin.
Asked then about prosperity, or what is lost or what is to come, the virgin or the boy tells everything.
The six-syllable mantra, with the heart at the end, becomes the eight-syllable mantra. There are other mantras of Ganesha in the tantra, O divine sage,
but whatever cannot be accomplished by practitioners in the three worlds with the twenty-eight- and the six-syllable ones, one would not see anywhere.
This procedure for the Ganesha mantras has been told to you by me; do not tell it to rogues, to others' disciples, or to deceivers.
The one who worships thus the god Ganesha, giver of all success, obtains all enjoyments here and at the end goes to the place of liberation.
He should make three circles on the ground, extending east-west. Standing in the western circle, with the worship materials in the middle,
and placing the Moon in another circle with a lotus, he should worship it properly by rule, preceded by worship of the seat.
The mantra-knower should place a silver vessel in front, fill it with cow's milk, and touching it chant the mantra
a hundred and eight times; then with the vidya-mantra he should offer arghya to the Moon, for success of all desired aims.
Doing this by this rule each month, unwearied, a man on earth obtains his desire within a year.
O Vidya, Vidya-malini, ... Chandrini, ... Chandramukhi — this is declared the Vidya mantra.
